target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 K → 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 → Def2 𝓢 K →
    Def5 𝓑 F →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (F φ 🡒 φ)) →
    ∃ ψ, 𝓢 ⊢ K ψ ⋏ K (∼F ψ)
translation: Target is the proposition stating that for all types Fm (sentences), S₀, and S (proof systems), equipped with formal logical connectives (implication 🡒, conjunction ⋏, disjunction ⋎, negation ∼), logical constants (⊤, ⊥), and provability relations on Fm for S₀ and for S; for all proof systems 𝓑 : S₀ and 𝓢 : S that each prove all classical propositional tautologies in these connectives and are closed under modus ponens; and for all arbitrary functions K, F : Fm → Fm from sentences to sentences, if the following five hypotheses hold: (1) Def1 𝓑 K: for every sentence φ : Fm, if 𝓑 proves φ, then 𝓑 proves K φ; (2) 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢: every sentence provable in 𝓑 is provable in 𝓢; (3) Def2 𝓢 K: for all sentences φ, ψ : Fm, 𝓢 proves K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ); (4) Def5 𝓑 F: there exists a sentence ψ : Fm such that 𝓑 proves ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ) (that is, (ψ 🡒 ∼(F ψ)) ⋏ (∼(F ψ) 🡒 ψ)); and (5) for every sentence φ : Fm, 𝓢 proves K (F φ 🡒 φ); then there exists a sentence ψ : Fm such that 𝓢 proves the conjunction K ψ ⋏ K (∼(F ψ)). Nothing else is assumed about the systems or functions: in particular, neither 𝓑 nor 𝓢 is required to be consistent, K and F are arbitrary functions on Fm with no further conditions (such as Def3, Def4, or Def6, or closure of 𝓢 under φ ↦ K φ, or distribution of K in 𝓑), and the existentially quantified sentence ψ in the conclusion is not stated to be the same sentence as the witness from Def5 𝓑 F.

divergences.description: Arithmetic, Robinson's Q, first-order quantifiers, Gödel numbering, and syntactic formulas with one free variable are not modelled: Fm is an arbitrary type with classical propositional connectives, 𝓑 and 𝓢 are arbitrary classical propositional systems, and K and F are arbitrary functions Fm → Fm. In particular, rather than deriving the diagonal equivalence s ↔ ¬F[s] from T including Q, the Lean statement assumes the existence of a Gödel fixed point for ∼F over 𝓑 (Def5 𝓑 F) as an explicit hypothesis. This idealization is declared in the author's claim.

Def1 𝓑 K (∀ φ, 𝓑 ⊢ φ → 𝓑 ⊢ K φ) assumes closure of the base theory 𝓑 under full (arbitrarily iterated) necessitation, which together with 𝓑 ⪯ 𝓢 and Def5 𝓑 F forces 𝓢 to prove K^n φ for every n and every 𝓑-theorem φ (including tautologies and the fixed-point equivalence). While this holds for the full epistemic base system of P-R323, it is a slightly stronger hypothesis than the minimal requirements noted in Reinhardt's remark in P-R324 (distributivity over implication plus a single application of B to tautologies and elementary axioms of arithmetic and equality, which would only require ∀ φ, 𝓑 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ K φ). Neither Bp → p nor Bp → BBp is assumed, matching the claim.

The formalization is slightly more general than the source in quantifying over arbitrary sentence types, proof systems, and functions K, F, and in requiring distributivity of K over implication (Def2) only in 𝓢 rather than also in the base theory 𝓑.

judgement.summary: The TARGET faithfully captures the abstract propositional-modal content of case (i) of Reinhardt's Theorem 1 without assuming Bp → p or Bp → BBp. The only caveats are the declared abstraction away from arithmetic and Gödel numbering (taking the diagonal fixed point as a hypothesis Def5 𝓑 F) and the slightly stronger use of iterated necessitation in 𝓑 (Def1 𝓑 K) rather than a single layer of K.
